elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The insertion reads "no more than once per year," which is anchored to a year rather than "any 12-month period"; on its face it would not prevent inspections in, e.g., December and the following January. To reach the preferred element the drafter must render the cap as "no more than once in any twelve (12) month period."

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Retained: "may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company" — written notice of at least 30 days.
Retained: "during the Company's normal business hours."

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection is performed by "HDI's General Manager" — a Vendor-side individual, not an independent auditor. No operative language substitutes an independent third-party auditor.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4 as rendered contains no confidentiality undertaking applicable to the inspecting person; nothing in the edit adds one.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No location provision; the clause is silent on off-site review of records and the redline adds none.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI" — unconditional Vendor cost-bearing, which is at least as favourable as cost-shifting only above a 5% underpayment.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The right is confined to inspecting "the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments" during business hours; no systems, remote-access or on-line access right is granted anywhere in the cited clause, so the condition sought (no direct system access) is satisfied on the operative text.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "have the right, no more than once per year, to inspect the records..." — an express annual frequency cap on HDI's inspection right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Retained: "no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company" exceeds the 15-day fallback threshold.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI" — Vendor bears cost with no shift-back trigger at all, which satisfies the fallback.

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the single inserted frequency cap supplies the only missing fallback element, and the retained 30-day written notice and unconditional HDI-borne inspection fees already exceed the 15-day and 10%-underpayment fallback thresholds.

Preferred level is not complete: no independent auditor, no auditor confidentiality obligation, no off-site-where-possible language, and the frequency cap is expressed as "once per year" rather than "in any twelve (12) month period" (which leaves a rolling-window gap allowing two inspections within 12 months). These are noted rather than pressed, consistent with the fallback-level target.

Minimality holds: the redline is one short parenthetical insertion ("no more than once per year,") placed grammatically within the existing sentence; no favourable retained language (30-day notice, business-hours limit, records-only scope, HDI-borne fees) was deleted or paraphrased, and no extras (survival, procedures, expense or damages language) were added.

Intent preserved: the inspection right remains confined to payment-calculation records of the Company's General Manager, the cost allocation and notice mechanics are untouched, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling ("HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined)" survives intact).

Deviation status is correct at the claimed fallback target because the unamended clause imposed no frequency limit at all; if the drafter wants the frequency element to hold under a rolling measure as well, change "once per year" to "once in any twelve (12) month period".
